title: Segment-Wise Accumulation: Low-Error Logarithmic Domain Computing for Efficient Large Language Model Inference
problem: Logarithmic domain computing reduces quantization error and computational complexity for LLMs but faces a precision-versus-hardware-overhead trade-off in multiply-accumulate operations requiring expensive high-precision logarithmic adders.
motivation: LDC is promising for efficiency but practical deployment requires balancing accumulation error with reasonable hardware cost; existing approaches require excessive precision overhead.
method: Proposes segment-wise accumulation (SWA) decomposing results into segments to mitigate LDC errors; introduces a processing element enabling SWA integration into systolic array architectures with lower overhead than floating-point enhancements.
key_novelty: Segment-wise accumulation strategy enabling low-precision logarithmic computing without equivalent hardware overhead.
contributions: Error analysis identifying accumulation as the critical LDC error source in LLMs
SWA technique providing error mitigation with minimal architectural changes
PE design for seamless systolic array integration
13.9% average accuracy improvement on LLAMA-2-7B with 24.6% area and 42.3% power reduction versus integer computing
limitations: Evaluation limited to LLAMA-2-7B; scalability to larger language models and other architectures not addressed.
